sources.rationale: QuerySet.filter reads rows back out of the ORM store; a value a request handler previously persisted re-enters the program attacker-chosen across requests. Paired with Model.save via the django-orm store key.
DB-API fetchone returns a row previously written with cursor.execute INSERT parameters; stored attacker text re-enters here. Paired with the execute write half via the sql-rows store key.
Batched form of fetchone: every row in the result set carries whatever earlier requests persisted, so the whole return value is stored attacker text under whole-value granularity.
psycopg2's cursor class lives at psycopg2.extensions.cursor; fetchall returns rows whose values earlier execute(query, vars) calls persisted — the PostgreSQL half of the sql-rows pairing.

redis.Redis.get(name) returns the bytes a previous set(name, value) stored; a cache or session value written from request data comes back attacker-chosen. Paired with Redis.set via the redis-kv store key.

pickle.loads is where a persisted blob re-enters the object graph: every value inside the unpickled result is whatever pickle.dumps serialised earlier, so the return is stored attacker data under whole-value granularity.

sinks.rationale: Model.save persists the instance's fields; a tainted field taints the instance under whole-value granularity, so a save of attacker text makes every later QuerySet read of the django-orm store attacker-controlled.

Attacker text bound as execute parameters is the SAFE way to run the statement and still persists that text: parameterisation stops sql-injection but not second-order storage. In the unbound spelling this entry matches (cursor, sql, parameters), the parameters sit at position 2 — a distinct claim from the statement position the sqli entry covers.

psycopg2 execute binds its vars argument server-side — injection-safe, storage-unsafe: bound attacker text lands in the table and re-enters through the paired fetchall read. Position 2 in the unbound spelling this entry matches (cursor, query, vars).
redis.Redis.set(name, value) persists the value argument (position 2 in the unbound spelling, keyword value= otherwise); attacker text stored here comes back verbatim through the paired Redis.get.
pickle.dumps is the serialisation boundary where attacker data enters a persisted blob; whatever is pickled here is exactly what the paired pickle.loads read hands back later.

Unpickling attacker bytes executes attacker-chosen reduce callables during load — code execution, not just data. This claim is about the INPUT being tainted; the stored_read entry for the same callee is about the OUTPUT being stored data.
